# Piyatara Sutta (Ud 5.1 (PTS Ud 47))

**ID:** Ud 5.1 (PTS Ud 47)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)

**Title (Pali):** Piyatara Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Piyatara Sutta* is the opening discourse of the fifth chapter of the *Udāna* (Ud 5.1, PTS Ud 47). In this sutta, King Pasenadi of Kosala asks Queen Mallikā whether there is anyone dearer to her than herself. When she confesses that no one is dearer to her than her own self, and the king agrees for himself, the matter is brought before the Buddha, who pronounces the solemn utterance (*udāna*): searching all directions with the mind, one finds no one dearer than oneself; recognizing that the self is similarly dear to others, one who loves oneself should not harm another [Pa-Auk Sayadaw].

Within the Pali canon, the sutta directly parallels the *Mallikāsutta* of the *Kosala Saṁyutta* (SN 3.8). Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this close relationship, showing that the core narrative and verses (§1.3–6.4) match SN 3 (§8.1.2–8.4.4) with 0.98 similarity [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records formulaic phrase matches with various discourses in the *Majjhima*, *Dīgha*, *Aṅguttara*, and *Saṁyutta Nikāyas* (such as MN 90, MN 86, and DN 16), as well as internal citations in the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. The text is furthermore referenced in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37).

Beyond Pali literature, verse and passage-level parallels are preserved across northern Buddhist traditions, including Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 5 / UVS 5 Priyavarga, Tibetan Uv Kg 5) and Chinese translations (T 212.6 and T 213.5). In contemporary Theravāda literature, the Buddha's verse from the sutta is cited by Pa-Auk Sayadaw as a scriptural basis for developing universal goodwill and non-violence toward other beings [Pa-Auk Sayadaw].
